title: Review: Reactivity series and displacement; Halide ions; Empirical and molecular formulae; Ideal gas equation and gas laws; Balanced equations and reacting masses; Concentration and standard solutions; Molar gas volume and Avogadro's law; Titrations and solution calculations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM03#t1 term and clue written for the game; AM08#t2 term and clue written for the game; AM03#t3 term and clue written for the game; AM03#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM03#N.11, AM05#N.7a, AM07#N.12a, AM08#N.11, AM05#N.9, AM07#N.14, AM08#N.13, AM05#N.10a, AM08#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Concentration
items.clue: Amount of solute divided by the volume of the whole solution.

items.label: Conical flask
items.clue: Vessel in which the two solutions meet, swirled over a white tile.

items.label: Volumetric flask
items.clue: Glassware filled until the bottom of the meniscus sits on the mark.

items.label: Dilution
items.clue: Adding water, which changes the volume but not the amount of solute.

questions.stem: Seawater contains about 1.29 g of magnesium ions, Mg²⁺, per dm³. How many moles of Mg²⁺ are in 250 cm³ of seawater? Data: Ar Mg 24.3.

Magnesium reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). What volume of hydrogen, in cm³ at RTP, forms from 0.120 g of magnesium? (Ar: Mg 24.3; molar gas volume 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹ at RTP)

Iron is produced by reducing iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g). What is the maximum mass of iron that can be produced from 40.0 g of iron(III) oxide? (Ar: O 16.0, Fe 55.8)

Now the mission: vinegar. 10.0 cm³ of vinegar is titrated with 0.500 mol dm⁻³ NaOH, using phenolphthalein. The mean titre is 16.60 cm³. CH₃COOH(aq) + NaOH(aq) → CH₃COONa(aq) + H₂O(l). What is the concentration of ethanoic acid in the vinegar, in mol dm⁻³?
questions.explanation: n(NaOH) = 0.500 × 0.01660 = 8.30 × 10⁻³ mol. Ratio 1 : 1, so 8.30 × 10⁻³ mol of acid. Divide by the vinegar volume, 0.0100: 0.830.

questions.stem: In the molar gas volume experiment, a student uses magnesium ribbon with a thin oxide coating that has not been cleaned off. How does this affect the calculated molar gas volume?

options.text: It is too high, because the oxide reacts with the acid to make extra gas.
It is too low, because part of the mass weighed gives no hydrogen.
It is unchanged, because the acid is in excess and all the solid reacts.
It is too high, because the calculated amount of magnesium is too large.

questions.explanation: n(Mg) is calculated from the full mass, but some is MgO. Less H₂ forms than expected, so V ÷ n is too small.

questions.stem: A strip of magnesium burns brightly in air and leaves white magnesium oxide: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s). What mass of MgO forms from 2.43 g of Mg? (Ar: O 16.0, Mg 24.3)

A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of a weak acid, HA, with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. The student then titrates an identical 25.0 cm³ sample of HA to which 50.0 cm³ of distilled water has been added. How does the volume of NaOH needed to reach the equivalence point compare with the first titration, and why?

options.text: It increases, because the flask now holds a larger volume of solution
It is unchanged, because the moles of HA in the flask are unchanged
It decreases, because the HA in the flask is now more dilute
It is unchanged, because adding water does not alter the pH

questions.explanation: Water changes the volume and concentration in the flask, not the moles of HA. The same moles of NaOH, so the same volume, are needed.

questions.stem: Two identical flasks at the same temperature and pressure are filled, one with neon, Ne, and one with sulfur hexafluoride, SF₆, a dense gas used in electrical switchgear. The SF₆ flask holds 7.2 times the mass of gas. Which statement is correct? (Ar: F 19.0, Ne 20.2, S 32.1)

options.text: The SF₆ flask holds 7.2 times as many particles as the neon flask.
The neon flask holds more particles, because neon atoms are much smaller.
Both flasks hold the same number of particles; each SF₆ molecule is about 7.2 times heavier.
Both flasks hold the same number of atoms, so there are 7 times as many Ne atoms as SF₆ molecules.

questions.explanation: Avogadro's law: same V, T and p → same number of particles. 146.1 ÷ 20.2 = 7.2.

questions.stem: Limewater is a solution of calcium hydroxide. Ca(OH)₂(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l). 25.0 cm³ of limewater is titrated with 0.0500 mol dm⁻³ HCl, using phenolphthalein. The mean titre is 18.40 cm³. What is the concentration of calcium hydroxide, in mol dm⁻³?
questions.explanation: n(HCl) = 0.0500 × 0.01840 = 9.20 × 10⁻⁴ mol. One Ca(OH)₂ reacts with two HCl: n = 4.60 × 10⁻⁴ mol. Divide by the sample volume, 0.0250: 0.0184.
